title: Use one numbered Sentry catalog across game and labs; retire old tower models
context: The owner named the Sentry lab as the reference and specified radial numbering: Rotor, Plasma, Quiver, Relay, Mortar, Lancer, Howitzer, Heptapod. Impact still exposed classic weapon profiles, the range contained three extra families, and Friendly units used procedural towers without starting the authored Sentry preload. This instruction explicitly retires the classic regression roster retained during migration.
outcome: src/content/sentries.js now owns numbers 1–8, labels, model IDs, sound-cue identity and radial order. Game radial, order/upgrade HUD, codex, Sentry/Impact/Audio selectors and Friendly units share these identities. Friendly opens on Rotor, loads actual game Sentry GLBs, and previews patterns using the shared weapon kinds. Removed the classic roster, dotted/solid tower factories, head tuner and obsolete tower geometry; preserved the two organic enemy forms exactly. Removed Needle/Kiln/Railgun tiers and the old standalone Heptapod (10 GLBs). Retained 24 Sentry tier models and four Terraformer states with pinned hashes. Removed three unused sound samples, renamed five still-used generic samples without changing their bytes, and updated the audio build recipe so retired outputs cannot return. Each Sentry has an independent fire cue using the same sample as its lab reference. Existing combat values and Mortar hack gating remain unchanged. Retired roster links normalize to roster 2; unknown Sentry-family links resolve to Rotor. FX base is now stalheart-fx-2: old exports are explicitly rejected because their weapon and cue keys differ. Recreate edits in the current labs before export/promotion. Current instructions, STATE and docs/SENTRIES.md describe this baseline; historical records remain immutable.
alternatives: Keep the classic roster and procedural tower tuner as compatibility variants: rejected by the owner’s explicit cleanup direction.
Number each UI independently: rejected because the radial, lab and unit catalog had already drifted.
Silently coerce old FX exports: rejected because retired profiles and renamed audio keys would lose or redirect edits without an explicit contract.
evidence: npm test: 64 test programs passed, including exact catalog/model inventory, model loading marker, combat, assets, preset promotion and existing game rules.
Compared all pre-cleanup Sentry combat fields against /tmp/stalheart-current-sentries.json: exact equality; organic enemy point sets also matched the pre-cleanup snapshot.
npm run check: syntax, 14 pure-layer modules, kernel provenance, logs, FX base and all 28 pinned Sentry/Terraformer assets passed. bash -n scripts/audio-build.sh passed; samples were not re-encoded.

Full source and nested-path release browser matrices passed: game boot, sector solvency, Sentry simulation, numbered mobile radial, input, rescue/raid, all hacking games, all three Terraformer hulls and damage transitions, labs and preset/audio round trip.

Final release authoring matrix passed on build d6b68222: selected all eight actual GLBs in Friendly, Sentry and Impact; retired roster URL normalized; audio edits reached explicit game preview while normal game content stayed isolated; PWA controlled the release page. Artifacts: artifacts/browser-dist/.

Browser-test failures during implementation were harness assumptions: retired roster expectations, hidden unrelated select element, lil-gui index values, duplicate radial digit badges, and same-URL navigation. Fixed selectors/navigation, removed duplicate badges, and reran successfully.
Visual review: numbered radial screenshot and Friendly 8. Heptapod screenshot show the requested labels and authored model.
npm run build: d6b68222, 384 files, 62,741,163 bytes. No deployment or remote push.
